questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I chose my study destination based on the appeal of the NYU campus which lies centrally in NYC. 
I had also heard that the university has good professors. 
I also wanted to go somewhere where the main language was English.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Difficult and confusing. However, once I was there it became a lot easier.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Online seminar with information and an in person introduction to visa guidelines.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky to know a friend of a friend. But housing in NYC is difficult and some of the other exchange students had to move during the program.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it is preferable, since the students living in dorms will most likely be a lot younger, and there is a mandatory meal plan that you have to sign up for. I was offered housing since I was on the waitlist but decided to decline since i had found another option.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: NYU has a lot of portals and it can be confusing. There is also a lot of information that you have to process and understand when you register.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They have an application portal where you fill out your details.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could email the offices of global services.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes that I wanted, however, I was not able to see which courses I could take until quite late. I think they have made the courses publicly available through the Albert Portal.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend that you look into what courses you can take well in advance and also what prerequisites they require and what days the courses are offered.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Mostly good professors and few students in each course.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were about the same level as UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some of the mid-terms and exams were multiple choise or short answer quizzess and in person essays. Generally, there is a higher level of monitorization with attendence for courses and weekly assignments about the readings.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
The Social Challenges of Climate Change
American Capitalism in Theory and Practice
Social Networks

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Both The Social Challenges of Climate Change and Social Networks. 
The professors were sweet and engaging. And the course material was interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Everything is more expensive in NYC.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: For instance, groceries are expensive. Insurance was also expensive. I would look into finding different insurance than the one NYU offers. You should do this before the end of September when you get there if you are going in the fall semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They are mainly focused on students who permanently are at NYU. But the Offices of Global Services offers some good opportunities for international students that I would recommend. We went to the UN building.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports, good gym facilities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Explore NYC, the city has a lot to offer.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Stay in NYC, there are always more areas to explore. I went to Montreal over the Thanksgiving break to visit a friend, this was also a good trip.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people in your courses. I made a few friends this way and they are willing to talk.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the language, both in lectures and the polite phrases used in other situations.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity of the city. I was able to seek out a community that I am normally not able to find as easily in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Apply for your visa well in advance! You need a bank statement amongst other things when you are applying. Check out courses in advance too. And everything will be fine and a lot easier practically once you get there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check out the courses on Albert.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends with other exchange students and students from NYU.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: There is 6-hour time difference between Copenhagen and NYC, this was a bit challenging if you needed to talk to somebody at home. It was also difficult not being able to go home for a short amount of time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
